title: M65, NGC 3623
caption: The spiral galaxy M65, imaged by the WIYN 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This image shows M65, also cataloged as NGC 3623, an Sa-type spiral galaxy in the constellation Leo. The field shown is 7.9 by 11.9 arcminutes.
M65 lies at a distance of about 35 million light-years. It appears to form a trio with two neighbors, the galaxies M66 and NGC 3628, which share its part of the sky.

Spiral galaxies are sorted into types by the size of their central bulge and how tightly their arms are wound. Type Sa galaxies sit at one end of that range, with a relatively large, bright bulge and smooth, tightly wrapped arms. Galaxies grouped together like M65 and its companions are bound by gravity, and over long spans of time their mutual pull can tug on one another's shapes and stir up gas. Small groups such as this are common, and our own Milky Way belongs to one too.
scale: M65 is about 35 million light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: The WIYN 0.9-meter telescope at Kitt Peak recorded M65 in visible light. The filters and color mapping are not published.
understand.eye: Through a small telescope M65 is a faint elongated smudge. The camera's exposures gather enough light to show the galaxy's structure.
